correctness.rationale: The modal normal form follows by induction and a depth-one characteristic formula. Local-injectivity and unique-class-palettes are precisely the singleton separation condition. Coefficient enumeration double-counts the successful labeled frame-color pairs directly. Pair and triple moments of a random set partition are exact by prescribed Bell identifications; Bell ratios give H_n/(nW(n))->1/2. The within-class color-collision indicators have a vertex-sharing dependency graph, whose Stein--Chen error is O(E sum |C|^3 /Q^2)=O(1/n) at Q~nW(n)); singleton singleton cross-class palette collisions contribute O(W(n)^2/Q) and all other cross-class pairs O(n^2/Q^2). The Poisson law and both tail regimes follow; no extrapolation from finite checks is used. The standalone verifier checked more than one million small frame-color combinations, exact census and direct closures; finite checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: Fully observable random finite S5 models are a natural question complementary to almost-sure frame validity: can random propositional data distinguish every world by formulas? The exact closed coefficient counts all labeled successful instances, the depth-one collapse makes expressive power transparent, and the sharp n log n Bell-scale transition with Poisson limit is a nontrivial effect of random partition structure. The result establishes both finite quantitative enumeration and a complete limiting threshold, not merely a renamed textbook birthday bound.
